goal: Build the trust foundation for the v5 redesign before adding new AI surfaces. Three independent backend slices: (1) extend the reconciliation decision vocabulary to skip and uncertain so the AI admits when it doesn't know, (2) stream the capture response so the user watches the AI work, (3) add templated AI narration on the existing event log so the agent's actions are described in plain English. None of these change the user-facing data model; they change the AI's behavior at the source and make that behavior legible in real time. After Phase 1 the user should feel the AI is more honest and more inspectable, which is the prerequisite for Phase 3's Ask ✦ and Memory view.
userProblem: The AI is too noisy at the source: low-confidence candidates default to 'new' (line 152 of v4_reconciliation.py), so the suggestion queue fills with low-quality 'maybe?' suggestions. The user can't see what the AI did during capture — the response is fire-and-forget with a 5-30s gap. The agent_activity log shows raw event types ('ai_updated at 14:32') instead of plain English ('I created task X from your note'). Combined, these mean the user either trusts the AI blindly (risky) or reviews every suggestion exhaustively (expensive). The redesign needs to address the trust deficit at the source, not by adding more UI chrome over a noisy output.
whyNow: These three changes are the prerequisites for the rest of the v5 redesign. Without skip/uncertain the Ask ✦ endpoint (Phase 3) will inherit the same noise problem. Without streaming capture the new capture sheet (Phase 2) will feel frozen during 30s LLM work. Without templated narration the new timeline view (Phase 3) will read as a log dump instead of a story. Tier 1 + 2 of the noise reduction work shipped on 2026-06-27 (untitled-fallback + gpt-5.4-nano + 4 extraction gating fixes); this phase is the next layer. The three slices are small, independent, and testable in isolation.

dataOrApiDependencies: Slice 1.1 (skip/uncertain) changes the default behavior of the reconciliation prompt and the auto-create threshold. Existing tests that assert on 'new' actions for low-confidence candidates must be updated to assert 'skip' or 'uncertain' instead.

Slice 1.2 (streaming) changes the capture response shape from a single JSON to a stream of events followed by a final JSON. Plan: a query param ?stream=true opt-in for the new behavior; the existing JSON response stays for callers that don't opt in.

tasks.title: Add skip and uncertain to reconciliation decision vocabulary
tasks.description: Currently the reconciliation LLM picks one of {new, update, link} per candidate, and the default is 'new' (v4_reconciliation.py line 152). This means a low-confidence 'Mary mentioned X' candidate gets suggested as 'create a new person Mary' even when there's a 30% chance the model is wrong. Extend the decision vocabulary to {new, update, link, skip, uncertain}. 'skip' = take no action, do not suggest. 'uncertain' = surface to the user for review with an explicit 'I wasn't sure' label. Default for low-confidence candidates becomes 'skip' instead of 'new'. Auto-create threshold drops from 0.9 to 0.85. The replay harness (scripts/replay_eval.py) is the safety net: run before and after, verify no regression on labeled 'expected: new' cases and ≥30% drop in suggestion count on the dismissed-creates fixture set.
acceptanceCriteria: services/v4_reconciliation.py prompt includes the new decision options skip and uncertain with explicit definitions
v4_reconciliation.py::_reconcile_candidates pads default decisions to 'skip' (not 'new') for low-confidence cases (confidence < 0.5)

tasks.title: Stream capture response via SSE (opt-in via ?stream=true)
tasks.description: POST /api/v4/capture currently blocks for 5-30s and returns a single JSON with applied_changes and suggestions. Add an opt-in streaming mode: when ?stream=true, the response is a Server-Sent Events stream with events: 'reading', 'extracting', 'candidates', 'reconciling', 'applying', 'linking', 'summarizing', 'done'. The existing single-shot response stays as the default for backward compat. The frontend's new capture sheet (Phase 2) will use ?stream=true to render live progress.

tasks.title: Templated AI narration on entity_events (read-side, cached)
tasks.description: entity_events rows have event_type and reason but no human-readable narration. Add a services/v4_narration.py module that generates a 1-sentence narration for each event_type via templates. Templates cover the 80% case; the remaining 20% fall back to a default. Surface as event.narration on /api/v4/entities/<id>/events responses. Generated on read, cached per event_id in memory (LRU 10k entries); no LLM call in the read path. This is the read-side companion to the existing entity_events writer; no writer changes.
